findings.description: No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects stored in this bucket are not encrypted at rest by default.

findings.issue_category: no bucket ACL / no access control defined
findings.description: No acl attribute is set (unlike other buckets in this file which explicitly set 'private'), so the bucket relies on the AWS default ACL, which combined with no explicit private setting is a weaker security posture and risks unintended public exposure.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined for this bucket holding sensitive ledger export data, leaving objects unencrypted at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket, so stored model artifacts are not encrypted at rest by default.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so operational runbook contents are stored unencrypted at rest.

The bucket uses the 'log-delivery-write' canned ACL which grants the log-delivery group WRITE and READ_ACP permissions; combined with force_destroy and its role as the audit log target, this broadens access beyond least privilege for an audit trail bucket.

This object is uploaded into aws_s3_bucket.reports_archive, which has no server-side encryption configured, so a vendor roster file (potentially containing sensitive vendor/PII data) is stored unencrypted at rest.
